Hi all —

Thanks for the loop. For clarity, Redwood's standard practice for POC/trial allowances is:

- We issue a formal credit memo (legal document) that reduces the customer's outstanding invoiced amount.
- For Redwood internal reporting the allowance is recorded as a contra-revenue (i.e., promotional discount) rather than a tax-deductible rebate. This keeps gross revenue intact and shows the promotional adjustment separately.

Practical implications for your GL team:
- Post the credit memo as a credit to Accounts Receivable and a debit to Promotional Allowances (contra-revenue / sales discounts).
- If you have separate revenue buckets, map Promo Allowances to 400-199 (or your equivalent contra-revenue code).

I've attached a sample credit memo PDF and a one-sheet with the recommended GL mapping for AP/AR. If Farside requires an alternative classification for local reporting (e.g., for EU VAT or local GAAP), let us know and we can provide supporting notes.

Attachments: Farside_TRIAL_CreditMemo.pdf (draft), promo-accounting-notes-jonas.xlsx
